name: System Design
description: Designing large-scale systems: scaling, caching, data stores, asynchronous processing and classic case studies.

nodes.name: Scalability basics
nodes.desc: Vertical versus horizontal scaling, stateless services, and where bottlenecks come from.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose between vertical and horizontal scaling, design stateless services and locate system bottlenecks.

nodes.name: Latency & throughput
nodes.desc: Latency numbers every engineer should know, throughput, percentiles and queueing intuition.
nodes.summary: You will be able to reason about latency and throughput using reference latency numbers, percentiles and basic queueing intuition.
topics: Latency numbers every engineer should know

nodes.name: Availability
nodes.desc: Availability nines, redundancy, failover, and SLIs, SLOs and SLAs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to quantify availability in nines, design redundancy and failover and define SLIs, SLOs and SLAs.
topics: Redundancy and single points of failure

nodes.name: Back-of-envelope
nodes.desc: Estimating QPS, storage and bandwidth for a design before drawing boxes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to estimate queries per second, storage and bandwidth for a system before designing it.

nodes.name: DNS & CDNs
nodes.desc: How DNS routes users, and serving static content from edge caches.
nodes.summary: You will understand how DNS resolves names to servers and how CDNs serve static content from edge caches close to users.

nodes.name: Load balancing
nodes.desc: L4 versus L7 balancers, balancing algorithms, health checks and sticky sessions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose between L4 and L7 load balancers and configure algorithms, health checks and session stickiness.

nodes.name: Proxies & gateways
nodes.desc: Reverse proxies, API gateways, service discovery and API design for services.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use reverse proxies and API gateways for routing, authentication and service discovery, and design service APIs.

nodes.name: Rate limiting
nodes.desc: Token bucket, leaky bucket and sliding-window limiters, local and distributed.
nodes.summary: You will be able to protect services with token bucket, leaky bucket and sliding-window rate limiters, locally or across nodes.

nodes.name: Caching
nodes.desc: Cache-aside, write-through and write-back, eviction policies, invalidation and hot keys.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose caching strategies, eviction policies and invalidation approaches and handle hot keys.

nodes.name: Databases at scale
nodes.desc: Choosing SQL or NoSQL, indexing, read replicas and the limits of a single database.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose between SQL and NoSQL stores, scale reads with replicas and recognise the limits of one database.

nodes.name: Replication
nodes.desc: Leader–follower and multi-leader replication, replication lag and read-your-writes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare leader-follower and multi-leader replication and handle replication lag and read-your-writes consistency.

nodes.name: Sharding
nodes.desc: Partitioning by key or range, consistent hashing and rebalancing.
nodes.summary: You will be able to partition data by key or range, use consistent hashing and rebalance shards as data grows.

nodes.name: CAP & consistency
nodes.desc: The CAP theorem, PACELC, and strong versus eventual consistency models.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply the CAP theorem and PACELC and choose between strong and eventual consistency models.

nodes.name: Object storage
nodes.desc: Storing files and media in object stores and serving them efficiently.
nodes.summary: You will be able to store files and media in object stores and serve them efficiently with signed URLs and CDNs.
topics: Object vs block vs file storage

nodes.name: Message queues
nodes.desc: Queues and logs (e.g. Kafka), producers and consumers, delivery guarantees and backpressure.
nodes.summary: You will be able to decouple services with queues and logs such as Kafka and reason about delivery guarantees and backpressure.

nodes.name: Event-driven design
nodes.desc: Pub/sub, event sourcing, CQRS and idempotent consumers.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design event-driven systems with pub/sub, event sourcing, CQRS and idempotent consumers.

nodes.name: Microservices
nodes.desc: Service boundaries, synchronous versus asynchronous communication, and their trade-offs against a monolith.
nodes.summary: You will be able to draw service boundaries and weigh synchronous and asynchronous communication against staying with a monolith.

nodes.name: Consensus
nodes.desc: Leader election, quorums, Raft at a high level, and distributed locks.
nodes.summary: You will understand how distributed nodes agree through leader election, quorums and Raft and how distributed locks work.

nodes.name: Distributed txns
nodes.desc: Two-phase commit, sagas and the outbox pattern.
nodes.summary: You will be able to keep data consistent across services with two-phase commit, sagas and the outbox pattern.

nodes.name: Observability
nodes.desc: Logs, metrics and traces, alerting, and debugging production systems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to instrument systems with logs, metrics and traces, set up alerting and debug production issues.

nodes.name: URL shortener
nodes.desc: Design a URL shortener end to end: estimates, API, ID generation, storage, caching and analytics.
nodes.summary: You will design a URL shortener end to end, covering estimates, API, ID generation, storage, caching and analytics.

nodes.name: Distributed limiter
nodes.desc: Design and prototype a distributed rate limiter backed by a shared cache, and load-test it.
nodes.summary: You will design and prototype a distributed rate limiter backed by a shared cache and load-test it.

nodes.name: Chat system
nodes.desc: Design a chat service: persistent connections, message fan-out, ordering, storage and presence.
nodes.summary: You will design a chat service covering persistent connections, message fan-out, ordering, storage and presence.

nodes.name: News feed
nodes.desc: Design a social news feed: fan-out on write versus read, ranking, caching and hot users.
nodes.summary: You will design a social news feed and weigh fan-out on write against fan-out on read, including ranking and hot users.
